```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

This guide runs `bionemor` on one Brev L40S instance. It uses BioNeMo
Framework 2.6.3 and public Evo 2 checkpoints from Hugging Face. The workflow
does not require an NGC key and does not start or test a NIM service.

The 7B smoke test covers diagnostics, generation, scoring, and raw logits. The
1B acceptance workflow covers public checkpoint conversion, baseline
inference, three full fitting steps, and fitted inference.

## Inspect before provisioning

Install and authenticate the Brev CLI, then run the provisioning script from
the repository root. It performs a dry run by default:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
./inst/scripts/brev-evo2-create.sh
```

The default type is `l40s-48gb.1x`. Brev availability and pricing can change,
so inspect the dry-run output and the current catalog before creating an
instance. There is no GPU-type fallback.

Create only after confirming the exact instance:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
./inst/scripts/brev-evo2-create.sh --create bionemor-evo2
```

## Run individual checks

Copy the repository and run the 7B smoke test:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
brev copy ./ bionemor-evo2:/home/ubuntu/bionemor/
brev exec bionemor-evo2 \
  "bash /home/ubuntu/bionemor/inst/scripts/brev-evo2-framework.sh"
```

Run the 1B fitting workflow:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
brev exec bionemor-evo2 \
  "bash /home/ubuntu/bionemor/inst/scripts/brev-evo2-finetune.sh"
```

The training phase has a hard 300-second container boundary. It includes FASTA
preprocessing and `train_evo2`. If it reaches the limit, the script removes the
training container and fails.

Stop the instance after individual runs:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
brev stop bionemor-evo2
```

## Opt-in acceptance runner

The explicit runner provisions, copies, runs both workflows, and stops the
instance from an `EXIT` trap:

```{bash, eval = FALSE}
./inst/scripts/brev-evo2-run.sh --run bionemor-evo2
```

`--run` is required because this action provisions billable compute. The trap
stops the instance after success or failure. Stopping preserves the converted
checkpoints and run artifacts on the instance disk.
